campbell.title: Campbell City Council — October 20, 2026
campbell.summary: The agenda for the Campbell City Council's October 20, 2026, meeting listed several recognitions, a routine consent calendar, a public hearing on extending deadlines for the Pruneyard Center expansion, and a lease for road-striping equipment. The agenda also included presentations honoring city code enforcement officers, a Little League championship team, and the new Youth Commission.
keyTopics: The agenda listed a public hearing on the Pruneyard Center Association's request to extend deadlines for Phases 3 and 4 of its master use permit, which cover a five-story office building, parking structure expansions, and additional commercial buildings. The request would also extend the related parcel map to December 31, 2031, for properties along S. Bascom Avenue and E. Campbell Avenue.
The agenda listed a proposed five-year lease with NCL Government Capital, totaling $159,327, for a thermoplastic melter trailer (a piece of equipment used for roadway striping and markings).

The consent calendar listed approval of $2,750,402.16 in bills and claims, along with a resolution adopting the city's job classification and salary schedules for fiscal years 2025-2026 and 2026-2027.

The agenda listed proclamations and recognitions for Code Enforcement Officer Appreciation Week (October 11-17) and the Campbell Little League Senior All-Star Team, listed as 2026 Northern California Senior League State Championship winners.
The agenda listed an introduction of the 2026-2027 Campbell Youth Commission, with commissioners presenting their initial work plan.

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — October 21, 2026
saratoga.summary: The agenda for the October 21, 2026, Saratoga City Council meeting listed routine business such as approving past meeting minutes and bill payments, along with final approval of two property splits. It also listed an annual update to the City Code and a proposal to start the process of creating a Climate Resilience District.
keyTopics: Approval of the minutes from the September 30, 2026, special meeting and the October 7, 2026, regular meeting
Acceptance of the vendor payment check registers dated 10/01/2026 and 10/08/2026
Final map approval to divide the property at 14860 Farwell Ave into two lots
Final map approval to divide the property at 18510 Sobey Rd into two lots

Public hearing on the annual City Code update, including changes to rules on scheduling appeals and qualifications for City Commissioners, plus a proposal to establish a Climate Resilience District Task Force and begin the process of creating a Climate Resilience District

los-altos.title: Los Altos City Council — October 27, 2026
los-altos.summary: The agenda for the October 27, 2026, Los Altos City Council meeting listed routine business such as minutes, an investment report, vehicle purchases, and two contracts for park and police building work. It also listed a proposed extension of a temporary moratorium on certain detention and custodial facilities, a Cal Water conservation presentation, and a proposed pay raise for the City Manager.
keyTopics: The agenda listed a $166,225 contract (plus up to 10% contingency) with Lignum Mellis of San Francisco to complete the Building B Park Expansion Project.
The agenda listed a $417,400 contract (plus up to 15% contingency) with ELECCO of Milpitas to replace the Police Department's backup generator.
The agenda listed an interim urgency ordinance to extend Ordinance No. 2026-548, a temporary moratorium on detention or custodial facilities and custodial processing facilities.

The agenda listed an amendment to the City Manager's employment agreement setting an annual base salary of $375,000 effective July 5, 2026, with a yearly CPI/general salary adjustment starting July 2027.

The agenda listed a Cal Water presentation on water conservation measures, a resolution on a Transit Signal Priority Policy on behalf of VTA, and a resolution to buy three replacement maintenance vehicles and one piece of equipment.

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — October 20, 2026
los-gatos.summary: The agenda for the October 20, 2026, Los Gatos Town Council meeting listed routine housekeeping items, including approval of minutes from two October 6 meetings and review of the Town's August financial reports. It also listed several items authorizing the Town Manager to sign or negotiate contracts and agreements, including an amendment with Foster and Foster, a three-year agreement, and a lease amendment.
keyTopics: Approval of the minutes from the October 6, 2026, Town Council Special Meeting and regular Town Council Meeting
Receipt of the August 2026 Expenditure and Revenue Reports and the Monthly Financial and Investment Report for August 2026
Approval and ratification of the Accounts Payable Check Registers and Payroll Report
A proposed first amendment to the Town's agreement with Foster and Foster, to be signed by the Town Manager
A proposed three-year agreement and a lease amendment that the Town Manager would be authorized to negotiate and execute

san-jose.body: Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole
san-jose.title: San José Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole — October 28, 2026
san-jose.summary: The agenda listed a San José Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole meeting on October 28, 2026, where members were set to review the final agenda for the November 3 City Council meeting and the draft agenda for November 10. Other listed items included a study session on improving affordability for residents, a report on City Council referrals from the past fiscal year, and an item on automated license plate readers.
keyTopics: The agenda listed a review of the November 3, 2026, final agenda and the November 10, 2026, draft agenda, including adding new items and assigning "time certain" slots to items if needed
A study session on Improving Affordability for San José Residents, presented by the City Manager
The Annual City Council Referral Status Report for Fiscal Year 2025-2026, from the City Manager
Retroactive approval of various Council District 8 special events as City Council-sponsored events, allowing the use of City funds and acceptance of donated materials and services (Candelas)
An item on Automated License Plate Readers, plus an appointment to the Deferred Compensation Advisory Committee

mountain-view.title: Mountain View City Council — October 27, 2026
mountain-view.summary: The agenda for the October 27, 2026, Mountain View City Council meeting listed a closed session at 5:15 p.m. on City Attorney employment matters, followed by a regular session at 6:30 p.m. The regular session agenda included youth recognitions, a proclamation, a presentation from the open space district, and items on a LinkedIn development agreement, housing bond financing, a freeway interchange design, the Public Safety Building bidding process, and a public art strategy.
keyTopics: Closed session listed at 5:15 p.m. covering labor negotiations and a public employee appointment for the City Attorney position
LinkedIn development agreement amendment for 700-810 East Middlefield Road and 1100-1200 Maude Avenue, listed for second reading
Tax-exempt bond financing for a multi-family housing project at 334 San Antonio Road
Design concept for State Route 237 and Middlefield Road interchange improvements (Project 19-65)
Public Safety Building (Project 20-49) pre-qualification for responsible bidders and subcontractors, plus a Public Art Strategy adoption item

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — October 27, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: The agenda for the October 27, 2026, Sunnyvale City Council meeting listed a 6 p.m. closed-session special meeting followed by a 7 p.m. regular meeting. Items before the Council included a nearly $3.3 million homeless services contract extension, a $7.4 million purchase of three new fire trucks, new 15 mph school zones, and changes to local rules on backyard housing and lot splits.
keyTopics: Homeless services contract: the agenda listed an amendment with WeHOPE for street outreach, the temporary hotel program, mobile hygiene services, and the inclement weather hotel program, raising the not-to-exceed amount to $3,255,267.36 (including contingency), extending the term through September 10, 2027, and approving a $2,152,098 budget modification.
Fire trucks: the Council was asked to authorize a $7,372,642.10 purchase order to Golden State Fire Apparatus, Inc. for three Pierce 100-foot tower fire apparatuses.

Housing and lot-split rules: a public hearing item proposed replacing the city's Dual Urban Opportunity (DUO) housing and Urban Lot Split chapters and updating related zoning and finance codes to conform with new state laws; the agenda lists it as exempt from CEQA.
School zones: a proposed resolution would establish 15 mph school zones and extend the school zone near Laurelwood Elementary School.
Water conservation: the agenda listed adoption of an ordinance prohibiting the use of potable water to irrigate nonfunctional turf, implementing state law AB 1572.

cupertino.title: Cupertino City Council — October 20, 2026
cupertino.summary: The agenda for the October 20, 2026, Cupertino City Council meeting lists proclamations, routine business items, two public hearings, and a discussion of how to lease a city-owned commercial property. A special meeting and study session were also noticed for 5:45 p.m. ahead of the 6:45 p.m. regular meeting; the agenda gives no details of what the study session covers.
keyTopics: The agenda listed a proposal to accept $850,000 in federal grant funds and award a design contract of up to $1,278,700 to Biggs Cardoza Associates, Inc. for the McClellan Road Bridge Project.

The agenda listed a proposed contract of up to $480,000 with Bay Aerials Gymnastics for city gymnastics classes and camps, with authority to extend two more years for a five-year total of up to $800,000.

A public hearing was listed on proposed updates to the Health and Safety chapter of the General Plan, along with changes to the noise and geologic/seismic appendices and a new Health and Safety Background Report.
A public hearing on conduit financing for The RISE Block 5 Apartments Project was listed, postponed from the October 6, 2026, meeting.
The Council was scheduled to consider a proposed approach for leasing the city-owned commercial property at 22100 Stevens Creek Boulevard.

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara City Council — October 20, 2026
santa-clara.summary: The agenda listed a special meeting of the Santa Clara City Council for October 20, 2026, at 5:30 p.m., held both in City Hall Council Chambers and virtually. It listed an update on the FIFA risk analysis disclosures investigation, along with several written requests from individual councilmembers asking to place items on future agendas, including topics on data centers and apartment parking.
keyTopics: The agenda listed an update on the FIFA Risk Analysis Disclosures Investigation.

Councilmember Hardy's request, deferred from October 6, asks that staff update the Council and public within 30 days on how new large electrical users, including data centers, get approvals and power allocations, with a possible moratorium on new stand-alone data centers.

Councilmember Hardy's second request, also deferred from October 6, asks for a future discussion of a policy that would bar the City from signing non-disclosure agreements with stand-alone data centers.

Councilmember Park's request, deferred from September 22 and October 6, asks for a future agenda item on how apartment residents could park near their complexes without fear of being ticketed or towed.

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — October 20, 2026
milpitas.summary: The agenda for the October 20, 2026, Milpitas City Council meeting listed routine business such as meeting calendars and minutes, along with a contract amendment for a new park design and a proposal to rename several community spaces. It also listed a presentation from the Santa Clara County Mosquito and Vector Control District and the annual report and work plans for the city's commissions.
keyTopics: The agenda listed a proposed $130,000 (not-to-exceed) amendment to the design contract with Callander Associates Landscape Architecture for the Metro Tango Subdistrict Park Project.

The agenda listed a resolution to rename the Cesar Chavez Community Garden the "Milpitas Community Garden" and Cesar Chavez Plaza the "Milpitas Civic Center Plaza," and to name the community garden in Delano Manongs Park the "Larry Itliong Community Garden."
The agenda listed a presentation from the Santa Clara County Mosquito and Vector Control District.

The agenda listed acceptance of the FY2025-26 Commission Annual Report and approval of FY2026-27 work plans for eight city commissions, including the Arts Commission and the Economic Development and Trade Commission.
The agenda listed routine items: the October and November 2026 meeting calendar, minutes from the October 6, 2026, meeting, and lists of upcoming and Councilmember-requested agenda items.

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto Architectural Review Board — October 15, 2026
palo-alto.summary: The agenda listed a public hearing before Palo Alto's Architectural Review Board on a request from AT&T to add new wireless equipment to two existing city-owned wood utility poles in the public right-of-way. The poles are near 670 Guinda Street and 754 Homer Avenue.
keyTopics: AT&T's request (file 26PLN-00229) to add new antennas, remote radio units, and associated equipment to two existing city-owned wood utility poles, treated as two Tier 2 wireless communication facilities
Proposed seven-foot fiberglass pole extensions on the poles, located near 670 Guinda Street and 754 Homer Avenue
Listed as a quasi-judicial public hearing, with the project marked exempt from environmental review under CEQA Section 15301 (Existing Facilities)
A supplemental report was added to the agenda packet for this item
